main.projectDescription: For one of my level 6 projects, I tasked myself with exploring different ways procedural generation could be done.

categories.categoryDescription: This is my attempt at creating Procedurally generating terrain, using chunks of landmass that load in and out around the player. I primarily experimented with mesh generation, but quickly saw the benefits of using Unity Terrain such as advanced texture splatmaps and automatic LOD meshing for further render distances.

cards.cardDescription: This is the main interface for this Terrain Chunk loader. You can set the dimensions and vertex density of the chunk, the textures to be used, the noise settings to get the type of terrain you want and the Render Terrain points to load chunks in and out depending on your coordinates. This script will procedurally generate landmass around the player, apply the terrain layers based on vertex height and minimalise chunk edge unalignment.
This is a working Terrain generator using simple Perlin noise to create hills and valleys.
I currently have a simple procedural texture mapper in my Terrain Chunk script, which applies 3 different layers of Terrain materials depending on vertex height.
I made a noise sampling script that allows the developer to input a list of instructions to get an output noise. This is an example of a specific noise setup that creates stalagmites.

During my terrain experiments, I realized that using the Unity Perlin function returnes symmetrical values past the x and y point. I created my own Perlin noise algorithm to combat this as shown in the other examples.
Each segment of terrain is loaded in and out using 'Render Terrain Points' where the developer can select what area around the player can load terrain in or deactivate out of bounds terrain.

categories.categoryDescription: I wanted to expand my knowledge on how certain types of mesh generation works. I started by looking at Convex Hull Mesh Generation, which is useful if you want to have a non-concave model. In these examples I used this tool to create rocks.

cards.cardDescription: This is a result of the Convex Hull Mesh Generation. This method of mesh generation is known as shrink-wrapping, since the mesh expands from a starting tetrahedron until it has no more points on the outside of the mesh.

This is the basic interface for creating your own Convex Hull Mesh. You can generate a mesh around a custom set of points or use the 'Generate points in Sphere/Cube' buttons to randomly place points. The Dot Tolerance controls how soft/sharp the final shape's edges are because it limits the angle it joins vertices to each other.
The output UVs are calculated using a Box-Mapping method, to try ensure as little amount of texture warping as possible.
High Dot Product example, and representation of the start of the process of Convex Hull Mesh Generation since it starts with a tetrahedron which then connects with all the outer points.
